q.intro.text: You are building a block-puzzle game. The L-block sits on a clear sheet pinned at P. The sheet makes a quarter turn clockwise about P.

q.ask.text: Which picture shows where the block lands?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the notation.

e.s1.text: The pin P is the center of the turn: the one point that stays still. Everything else goes around it.

e.s2.text: Corner A is three right, one up from P. Turn those steps like a pointer, a quarter turn clockwise: right turns into down, up turns into right. A prime is one right, three down.

e.s3.text: B and C turn the same amount, the same way, about the same pin. Each string from P keeps its length.

e.s4.text: Turn the whole sheet: the block lands exactly on A prime, B prime and C prime. Every side kept its length, and A, B, C still goes clockwise.

e.why.text: Quick check: why did corner C move so much farther than corner B?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. Everything turned the same quarter turn, but C is farther from the pin, so its circle is bigger.

e.w-arm.text: They turned the same amount: a quarter turn each. A longer string only makes a bigger circle.

e.w-slide.text: Nothing slid. The sheet only turned about P; C just sits farther out.

t.intro.text: Now a triangle on the sheet makes a quarter turn counterclockwise about P. The pin and corner A are done for you.

t.b-ask.text: B is two right, three up from P. Where does B land?

t.b-tap.text: Tap a dot in the picture, or pick it here.

t.b-ok.text: Yes: right turns into up, up turns into left. B prime is three left, two up.

t.b-rev.text: That is a quarter turn clockwise. Counterclockwise goes against the clock.

t.b-one.text: That turns only the two right and leaves the three up as it was. Both steps turn: three up turns into three left.

t.b-count.text: One step short: count the jumps between dots, not the dot you start on. three up turns into three left.

t.c-auto.text: C goes the same way: five right, one up turns into one left, five up.

t.k-ask.text: The sheet turns onto the new dots. What did the turn keep?

t.k-ok.text: Right: same sides, same corner order. The turn moved the triangle; it did not change it.

t.k-proto.text: It points a new way, but it is the same triangle: every side kept its length.

t.k-one.text: Every corner has to land right. Check B and C too, not just A.

t.cb-right.text: You were right: picture two. Now you can show why, corner by corner.

t.cb-center.text: Picture one turned about its own corner, not about the pin P. Every point must keep its distance from P: picture two.

t.cb-flip.text: Picture three is flipped down, a mirror image: A, B, C goes the other way round. The quarter turn is picture two.

t.cb-none.text: The quarter turn about P is picture two.

p.intro.text: Riley drew the L and a lavender L below line m, and says: it is upside down, so it is a half turn of the L.

p.build.text: Now prove it. Fill each “because” with the reason that makes the line true.

p.build-test.text: Let’s test it. Fill each “because” with the reason that makes the line true, and see where it leads.

p.claim1.text: A turn keeps A, B, C going the same way round,

p.claim2.text: In Riley’s picture A, B, C goes the other way round,

p.claim3.text: So Riley’s picture is a flip across m, not a half turn,

p.c1.text: Right. The sheet stays face up when it turns. Watch: a real half turn makes a different picture.

p.c2.text: Clockwise in the L, counterclockwise in Riley’s picture. No turn can do that.

p.c3.text: Fold the sheet over line m, and the L lands exactly on Riley’s picture. It is a flip.

p.x-upside.text: Upside down happens in a flip too. Trace the corners: the order tells a turn from a flip.

p.x-one.text: One corner is not enough. Every corner has to match.

p.x-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.done.text: That’s a proof: three claims, each with its reason, and the picture backs every one. Riley’s picture is a flip.
